retired.title: The compressor is retired
retired.body: Forge no longer compresses or rewrites request context. Context is append-only: editing earlier messages invalidates the model's KV cache prefix (a mid-history edit cut cache reuse to under 1% in measurements) and has caused silent corruption, while the compressor saved only about 2.5% of tokens. Forge now reduces how much context is created at the source instead (ADR-0017).
retired.status_bypassed: Every request is forwarded to its upstream unchanged.
retired.warn_not_bypassed: Warning: the global passthrough setting is off in the store, so a retired compressor proxy may still be on the request path. Turn it back on from the CLI (forge config set compressor.passthrough_all true).
retired.no_controls: There is no switch here to turn it back on. Re-enabling any message-rewriting hop requires an ADR-0017 amendment.
retired.proxies_note: These proxy rows are kept only so existing units can be cleaned up. No new proxies are created, and linking a provider no longer starts one.

self_review.toggle_label: Periodically re-check open investigations and parked actions
self_review.description: An investigation whose checks now read clean gets a closure proposal in the pending tray — approve it to actually close the investigation. A stuck "done, unverified" action is promoted to "done" automatically once its own checks re-verify clean (that's bookkeeping catching up to reality, not a new action); a pending proposal smith made on its own is superseded automatically once the condition it was about no longer applies.

brain_residency.description: Off (default): smith's brain is loaded on demand, only when a question actually needs the reasoning tier, and left to unload afterward per normal idle policy — no standing VRAM cost, but each first escalated question after an idle period pays a real load delay. On: smith proactively keeps the brain resident, permanently giving up its VRAM footprint in exchange for no per-question load latency. Either way, the brain is never pinned to a specific slot — the scheduler picks whichever is free.

autonomy.intro: Off by default. When enabled here, smith may carry out a specific, opted-in fix the moment it detects the problem — no click, no approval — instead of only ever proposing it for a human. Every autonomous run still goes through the same procedure engine (checkpoints, post-verify, full audit trail) as a manually-approved one, and is bounded by a cooldown plus a daily cap per procedure. Only procedures assessed as low-risk are ever eligible for this — the list below can't be widened from here.
autonomy.global_switch: Global switch — smith may run opted-in fixes unattended
autonomy.global_switch_note: The kill switch. Off always means nothing is autonomous, regardless of the per-procedure toggles below.

behavior.heading: Model Behavior
behavior.intro: A request's model name may resolve through an alias that forces its own defaults on every call through that name; capability-tier substitution (the toggle above) may then substitute an already-loaded config ranked in the same capability tier instead of waiting on a load; and reasoning_effort is translated per that config's own build — native passthrough where the build honors it directly, an injected enable_thinking kwarg where only that exists, or left alone where neither does. Mutations require admin + Settings assurance.
behavior.configs_note: One row per config. "native" under the thinking column means this build honors reasoning_effort directly and the override is unused; everything else is a build that only understands the enable_thinking chat-template kwarg (or nothing at all) — set Force on there to let reasoning_effort: none actually take effect on it.
behavior.tiers_note: Groups of configs that may substitute for each other under capability-tier substitution — an already-loaded model standing in for a requested one, to avoid a load wait or to prefer a smarter resident model. Curated, not derived: assign a config to a class and a rank (lower = more capable) in the table above or the config's own edit form. The global on/off mode is the Capability-tier substitution toggle on the Router behavior card above.
behavior.aliases_note: A second name for a config that FORCES a setting on every request through that name — even overriding what the caller asks for. For a consumer that can't send custom parameters itself (e.g. a fixed integration that can only be pointed at one model name), an alias guarantees the behavior it needs without a second, duplicate config.
behavior.virtual_models_note: A model name for a caller that doesn't care which real config serves it, only that it has some general characteristic — resolved to a real config fresh on every request, never a fixed target the way an alias is above. Capability-tier kind ranks a capability tier's own curated members; throughput kind ignores tiers entirely and ranks by real measured tokens/sec instead, so it's never a guess. Either way, whichever candidate is already loaded wins — otherwise the best-ranked one loads fresh, same as any other request.

danger.cookie_secure.label: Secure cookies
danger.cookie_secure.help: Secure attribute on the session + WebAuthn challenge cookies. Leave on unless this process is reached only over plain HTTP behind its own TLS-terminating reverse proxy on the same host (the tailscale-serve-only deployment model) — with it off, a session cookie can be replayed over any plaintext connection an attacker gets the browser to make. Unlike every other field in this section, this one takes effect immediately on save, no restart needed.

landmark.billing.cost.help: Electricity rate, overhead, PSU efficiency, power-chart ceiling — feeds the Dashboard's cost figures.

landmark.billing.currency.label: Currency
landmark.billing.currency.help: Display currency for every money figure in the PWA, plus the server-side FX source.

landmark.catalog.configs.label: Model catalog · Configs
landmark.catalog.configs.help: Local launch recipes — model + variant + engine build and flags (extra_args, context…).

landmark.catalog.models.label: Model catalog · Models
landmark.catalog.models.help: Parent models — weights, capabilities, modalities, logos.

landmark.catalog.notes.label: Model catalog · Notes
landmark.catalog.notes.help: Freeform operator notes attached to catalog entries.

landmark.catalog.services.label: Model catalog · Services
landmark.catalog.services.help: Managed always-on services (embeddings, STT, TTS) and their unit state.

landmark.catalog.taxonomy.label: Model catalog · Model Family
landmark.catalog.taxonomy.help: Genealogy/family taxonomy — names and icon inheritance hierarchy.

landmark.compressor.mode.label: Compressor routing mode
landmark.compressor.mode.help: Global passthrough toggle — bypass Compressor compression for every proxy, live, no teardown.

landmark.compressor.proxies.label: Compressor compression proxies
landmark.compressor.proxies.help: Per-proxy compression on/off, restart/teardown, tokens saved.

landmark.danger.restart.label: Restart daemon
landmark.danger.restart.help: Applies every restart-mode change immediately via D-Bus — does not unload models, drops in-flight a0 requests and SSE subscribers.

landmark.general.daemon_strip.label: Daemon status strip (read-only)
landmark.general.daemon_strip.help: Version, listen addresses, and the restart-required banner — informational, not editable.

landmark.profiling.index.label: Profiling
landmark.profiling.index.help: Destructive live profiling runs — depth sweep over context sizes on a real slot, evicting whatever is loaded.

landmark.providers.index.label: Providers & API keys
landmark.providers.index.help: External providers routed via a0 — endpoint, write-only key, preset, health.

landmark.routing.models.label: Model → provider routing
landmark.routing.models.help: Which provider a0 presents for each model, and the priority order a failover walks.

landmark.routing.preview.label: Routing map
landmark.routing.preview.help: Read-only provider→model dendrogram — link thickness encodes priority, color encodes active vs disabled.

landmark.scheduling.live.label: Scheduler tunables (live)
landmark.scheduling.live.help: The running scheduler.config — idle unload, small-job threshold, priority jump cap, reservation window. Mirrored on the Scheduling page.

landmark.security.auth_config.label: Auth configuration
landmark.security.auth_config.help: Network provider selection (tailscale / forward-auth header) and the embedded forward-auth Danger Zone.

landmark.security.policy.label: Access policy
landmark.security.policy.help: The resource → minimum-factor matrix — which actions need password, TOTP, or passkey assurance.

landmark.security.recovery.label: Recovery codes
landmark.security.recovery.help: One-time recovery codes for lockout — view/regenerate.

landmark.security.webauthn.label: Passkeys (WebAuthn)
landmark.security.webauthn.help: Passkey / hardware-key enrollment — the L2 assurance factor.

monitoring.gtt_warn_pct.label: Warn when GPU memory is this full
monitoring.gtt_warn_pct.help: Raise a memory-pressure warning when the GTT (GPU-visible memory) pool is filled past this percentage.

monitoring.hang_sustain_s.label: Hung only if slow for
monitoring.hang_sustain_s.help: How long generation must stay below that speed before a hang alert fires. A longer time avoids false alarms on slow prompts.

monitoring.hang_tps_thousandth.label: Flag a request as hung below
monitoring.hang_tps_thousandth.help: A request that is still processing but generating fewer tokens per second than this, for the duration set below, is flagged as hung. Default 0.1.

monitoring.poll_interval_s.label: Check slot metrics every
monitoring.poll_interval_s.help: How often the collector reads each loaded slot's metrics. Shorter means fresher charts and quicker hang detection, at slightly more load.

monitoring.retention_days.label: Keep metric history for
monitoring.retention_days.help: Older metric samples are deleted after this many days. Takes effect on the next cleanup.

monitoring.sample_interval_s.label: Record a metrics sample every
monitoring.sample_interval_s.help: How often a metric sample is saved to history. Needs a daemon restart to take effect.

monitoring.switch_cooldown_s.label: Minimum wait between model switches on a slot
monitoring.switch_cooldown_s.help: After a model switch, the same slot will not switch again until this much time has passed.

routing.busy_mode.label: Busy mode
routing.busy_mode.help: What a0 does when the target slot is busy loading/switching: wait for it, or fail fast.

routing.capability_substitution.label: Capability-tier substitution
routing.capability_substitution.help: Let an already-loaded, operator-ranked config stand in for a requested one — "Fallback only" substitutes just when the requested config is genuinely infeasible to load right now; "Prefer smarter" also substitutes whenever a loaded config outranks the requested one, even if loading it would have been feasible. A capability tier's own override (the Capability tiers card below, under Model Behavior) takes precedence over this default. Off by default — a request with no eligible substitute behaves identically either way.

routing.connect_timeout_s.label: Give up connecting to a backend after
routing.connect_timeout_s.help: How long a0 waits for a backend to accept a connection before treating it as down.

routing.embedding_url.label: Embedding URL
routing.embedding_url.help: Absolute http(s) URL for the embeddings backend a0 proxies to.

routing.ensure_loaded_timeout_s.label: Wait for an on-demand model load up to
routing.ensure_loaded_timeout_s.help: If a request needs a model that is not loaded, a0 loads it and waits this long; past that the request fails.

routing.health_ttl_s.label: Re-check backend health every
routing.health_ttl_s.help: A backend health result is reused for this long before a0 checks again.

routing.inject_stream_usage.label: Record real spend on streaming requests
routing.inject_stream_usage.help: Ask remote providers to append a usage summary to streamed replies, so actual API spend can be recorded. Local models are unaffected.

routing.max_retries_per_backend.label: Retries before trying another backend
routing.max_retries_per_backend.help: How many times a0 retries one backend before failing over to another or giving up.

routing.provider_failover.label: Provider failover
routing.provider_failover.help: When the preferred provider for a model errors (transport failure or 5xx), retry the next provider offering the same model, in priority order. Off = the error surfaces instead of silently spending on the next provider. 4xx responses never fail over.

routing.request_timeout_s.label: Request timeout
routing.request_timeout_s.help: 0 means unbounded, which is the default on purpose: a fixed timeout cuts long speculative-decode responses off mid-generation. A hung client or upstream is still caught when the connection drops.

routing.tts_url.label: TTS URL
routing.tts_url.help: Absolute http(s) URL for the forge-tts backend a0 proxies /v1/audio/speech and /v1/voices to (Tier 1 Sprint 3).

scheduling.seed.idle_unload_s.label: Unload idle models after (starting value)
scheduling.seed.idle_unload_s.help: Used only on a fresh boot when the live scheduler settings were never saved. Changing it does not affect the running daemon.

scheduling.seed.priority_jump_cap.label: How often a job may jump the queue (starting value)
scheduling.seed.priority_jump_cap.help: Cap on how many times a higher-priority job may jump ahead of waiting work. Starting value for a fresh boot.

scheduling.seed.reservation_soon_min.label: Treat a reservation as imminent within (starting value)
scheduling.seed.reservation_soon_min.help: A reservation starting within this many minutes counts as imminent, so the scheduler holds its slot. Starting value for a fresh boot.

scheduling.seed.small_job_token_threshol.label: Small-job size (starting value)
scheduling.seed.small_job_token_threshol.help: Requests at or below this many tokens count as small jobs. Starting value for a fresh boot; same rule as above.

security.forward_auth.header_name.label: Forward-auth header name
security.forward_auth.header_name.help: HTTP header the reverse proxy sets with the authenticated username, when network_provider is forward_auth_header.

security.forward_auth.trusted_cidrs.label: Trusted CIDRs
security.forward_auth.trusted_cidrs.help: Comma-separated CIDR ranges allowed to set the forward-auth header. The highest-value check in this app: a save that would exclude YOUR OWN address is refused outright, not just warned about — total lockout is not recoverable without direct database access.

smith.brain_chain.label: smith brain fallback chain
smith.brain_chain.help: Ordered local configs smith tries when it needs to escalate to a brain — a loaded, idle member answers with zero load wait, otherwise smith falls down the chain toward smith.model.

smith.build_refresh_watchlist.label: build-refresh watchlist
smith.build_refresh_watchlist.help: Keywords smith matches against fetched upstream commit subjects when a tracked build has drifted — a hit is surfaced regardless of the drift threshold.

smith.handoff_offerings.label: smith handoff offering order
smith.handoff_offerings.help: Ordered remote Offerings smith's self-eviction handoff probes when its brain's slot needs to be freed.

smith.model.label: smith brain model
smith.model.help: The Config or Offering smith calls via a0 when it needs to think. Empty or unresolvable means smith answers without a model.

smith.schedule.deep.label: Deep checks run every
smith.schedule.deep.help: How often smith runs its full check catalog, including slower network probes.

smith.schedule.quick.label: Quick checks run every
smith.schedule.quick.help: How often smith runs its quick checks.

smith.thresholds.build_refresh_behind_n.label: Build-refresh drift threshold
smith.thresholds.build_refresh_behind_n.help: How many commits a tracked build must drift behind upstream before smith proposes a rebuild. Below-threshold drift still shows as an info finding, it just doesn't propose a rebuild.

smith.thresholds.compressor_failopen_war.label: Compressor fail-open warn %
smith.thresholds.compressor_failopen_war.help: Fail-open rate threshold (%) — smith proposes raising the compressor fail-open budget when the 1-hour rolling rate exceeds this.

smith.thresholds.device_lost_window_minu.label: Device-lost detection window
smith.thresholds.device_lost_window_minu.help: How far back smith looks for a GPU device-lost event before treating it as resolved.

smith.thresholds.disk_crit_pct.label: Disk crit threshold
smith.thresholds.disk_crit_pct.help: Disk usage percentage at which smith's disk_space check reports crit.

smith.thresholds.disk_warn_pct.label: Disk warn threshold
smith.thresholds.disk_warn_pct.help: Disk usage percentage at which smith's disk_space check reports warn.

smith.thresholds.gtt_crit_pct.label: GTT crit threshold
smith.thresholds.gtt_crit_pct.help: GTT pool usage percentage at which smith's gtt_ceiling check reports crit.

smith.thresholds.gtt_warn_pct.label: GTT warn threshold
smith.thresholds.gtt_warn_pct.help: GTT pool usage percentage at which smith's gtt_ceiling check reports warn.

smith.web.api_keys.label: Web provider URLs and API keys
smith.web.api_keys.help: Base URLs and (optional) API keys for searxng and firecrawl.

smith.web.cache_ttl.label: Reuse web results for
smith.web.cache_ttl.help: How long a search or fetch result is reused before smith fetches it again.

smith.web.enabled.label: Web research enabled
smith.web.enabled.help: Master switch for web research (search + fetch). On by default — turn off to keep smith to local evidence only.

smith.web.provider_order.label: Web provider order
smith.web.provider_order.help: Preference order among the fetch-capable adapters (searxng only searches; direct is always tried last regardless of this order).

voice.base.enabled.label: Base / clone: enabled
voice.base.enabled.help: Whether the Base / clone engine participates at all. Disabled refuses every request for it outright instead of silently falling back.

voice.base.mode.label: Base / clone: mode
voice.base.mode.help: Always on keeps the engine running continuously (fast, standing GPU memory). On demand serves requests without a standing process (the per-request fallback; Kokoro has no such tier, so it behaves like Always on). Disabled refuses the engine outright. For an engine that runs in a dedicated slot this is that engine's own setting (Engines tab) and applies at once.

voice.base.unit.label: Base / clone: systemd unit
voice.base.unit.help: The systemd unit this engine's resident process runs as (e.g. forge-tts-custom, kokoro). Empty means the daemon doesn't manage a process for it — resident mode then has nothing to start, same effect as available.

voice.base.url.label: Base / clone: backend URL
voice.base.url.help: Where forge-tts reaches this engine's resident backend (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8091). Empty means not configured — falls back to the CLI path for the three Qwen sub-variants, or is simply unreachable for kokoro.

voice.base.pool_member.label: Base / clone: dedicated-slot engine
voice.base.pool_member.help: Run this engine in a dedicated slot (Engines tab). Its address then comes from that slot, the pool loads it, and the unit and address under Own process are ignored.

voice.customvoice.enabled.label: Custom voice: enabled
voice.customvoice.enabled.help: Whether the Custom voice engine participates at all. Disabled refuses every request for it outright instead of silently falling back.

landmark.catalog.builds.label: Model catalog · Builds & files
landmark.catalog.builds.help: Engine builds (llama.cpp, Radiance) and downloaded model files — register or retire a build, check binary paths.

landmark.security.hf_token.label: Hugging Face token
landmark.security.hf_token.help: The access token used to search and download models from Hugging Face (gated or private repos).

billing.display_currency.label: Display currency
billing.display_currency.help: The currency every money figure in the dashboard is shown in (ISO 4217 code).

billing.fx_source_url.label: Exchange-rate source URL (optional)
billing.fx_source_url.help: Web address the server fetches currency exchange rates from. Optional.

billing.fx_refresh_min.label: Refresh exchange rates every (optional)
billing.fx_refresh_min.help: How often exchange rates are re-fetched. Leave blank for the server default.

billing.rate_per_kwh.label: Electricity rate
billing.rate_per_kwh.help: What you pay per kilowatt-hour; used for every cost figure.

billing.rate_currency.label: Electricity rate currency
billing.rate_currency.help: The currency the electricity rate above is expressed in (ISO 4217 code).

billing.overhead_w.label: Rest-of-system power overhead
billing.overhead_w.help: Added to measured package watts, then divided by PSU efficiency to get wall watts.

billing.psu_efficiency.label: Power-supply efficiency
billing.psu_efficiency.help: Wall watts = (package watts + overhead) ÷ efficiency. An uncalibrated estimate until checked against a plug meter. Between 0.01 and 1.

billing.max_power_w.label: Overview power-chart ceiling
billing.max_power_w.help: Scales the Overview power chart and tile against the hardware’s real maximum draw (package watts). Never used in cost math.

billing.power_kw.label: Model-card power constant
billing.power_kw.help: A flat “if this model ran alone, flat-out” rate used only for power estimates on model and config cards. It does not feed measured energy figures.

validation.duration: Enter a number and pick a unit (for example 30 minutes).
